fact: Transformers process tokens simultaneously using self-attention instead of sequential recurrence.
Gradient descent updates model parameters by moving opposite the gradient of the loss.
ReLU became popular because it helps reduce the vanishing gradient problem.
CNNs learn edges before textures and objects.
Word embeddings place semantically similar words close together in vector space.
Supervised learning trains models on examples that include known target answers.
Unsupervised learning finds patterns in data without labeled target outputs.
Reinforcement learning trains agents through rewards, penalties, and interaction.
Neural networks learn by adjusting weights across connected layers.
Backpropagation computes how much each weight contributed to prediction error.
Language models predict likely next tokens from patterns learned during training.
A token can be a word, part of a word, punctuation, or whitespace.
Context windows limit how much text a model can consider at one time.
Attention weights help a transformer relate each token to other tokens.
Tokenization converts raw text into units that a model can process.
Part-of-speech tagging identifies grammatical roles such as nouns and verbs.
Named entity recognition detects names of people, places, organizations, and dates.
Image classification assigns a label to an entire image.
Object detection predicts both object categories and bounding boxes.
Image segmentation assigns a class label to individual pixels.
Optical character recognition converts text in images into machine-readable text.
Training data quality often matters as much as model architecture.
Label noise can reduce accuracy by teaching a model inconsistent patterns.
Data leakage occurs when training data contains information from the test target.
A test set estimates how well a model performs on unseen data.
Validation sets help tune models without touching the final test set.
Accuracy can be misleading when classes are highly imbalanced.
Precision measures how many predicted positives are actually positive.
Recall measures how many actual positives a model successfully finds.
F1 score balances precision and recall using their harmonic mean.
Overfitting happens when a model memorizes training data instead of generalizing.
Underfitting happens when a model is too simple to capture useful patterns.
Regularization discourages overly complex models that fit noise.
Cross-validation estimates performance by training and testing across multiple splits.
Dropout randomly disables units during training to reduce overfitting.
Batch normalization stabilizes training by normalizing layer activations.
Activation functions let neural networks model nonlinear relationships.
Sigmoid activations squeeze values into the range from zero to one.
Softmax converts raw class scores into probabilities that sum to one.
Learning rate controls the size of each training update.
A learning rate that is too high can make training unstable.
A learning rate that is too low can make training unnecessarily slow.
Adam combines momentum and adaptive learning rates for each parameter.
Momentum helps gradient descent keep moving through shallow or noisy regions.
Bias is systematic error from assumptions that are too simple or incorrect.
Variance is sensitivity to small changes in the training data.
The bias-variance tradeoff describes a balance between simplicity and flexibility.
Correlation does not prove that one variable causes another.
Bayesian methods update beliefs using evidence and prior assumptions.
Rule-based expert systems were an early form of practical artificial intelligence.
Search algorithms explore possible actions to find a goal state.
A* search uses both path cost and a heuristic estimate to guide exploration.
Minimax helps game-playing agents choose moves against optimal opponents.
Alpha-beta pruning skips game-tree branches that cannot affect the final choice.
An agent is the decision-maker in a reinforcement learning environment.
A policy maps observations or states to actions.
A reward signal tells an agent how good an outcome was.
Q-learning estimates the value of taking actions in states.
Exploration lets agents try actions that may improve future rewards.
Exploitation uses the best-known action based on current knowledge.
Generative models create new content that resembles their training data.
Diffusion models learn to reverse a gradual noise-adding process.
GANs train a generator and discriminator in a competitive setup.
Variational autoencoders learn compact latent representations for generation.
Prompt engineering shapes model output by changing instructions and context.
Temperature controls how random a language model's sampling can be.
Lower temperature usually makes generated text more predictable.
Higher temperature can produce more varied but less consistent text.
Top-p sampling chooses from the smallest token set with enough probability mass.
System instructions can define a model's role, constraints, and response style.
Few-shot prompting includes examples to demonstrate the desired pattern.
Zero-shot prompting asks a model to perform a task without examples.
Embeddings represent text, images, or other data as numeric vectors.
Cosine similarity compares vector direction rather than vector length.
Vector search retrieves items with embeddings close to a query embedding.
Semantic search can find related meanings even when exact words differ.
Clustering embeddings can reveal groups of similar documents or users.
Retrieval-augmented generation gives a model external context before answering.
Chunking splits long documents into smaller pieces for retrieval.
Reranking reorders retrieved results using a second scoring step.
Hybrid search combines keyword matching with vector similarity.
Grounding connects model responses to provided data or sources.
Hallucination is when a model produces unsupported or false information.
Alignment aims to make AI systems follow human goals and constraints.
Red teaming tests systems by actively searching for failures and misuse paths.
Guardrails add checks or constraints around model inputs and outputs.
Human-in-the-loop review keeps people involved in sensitive decisions.
Model cards summarize intended use, limitations, and evaluation results.
Bias in AI can reflect patterns and gaps present in training data.
Fairness metrics can disagree because different definitions optimize different goals.
Explainability helps people understand why a model made a prediction.
Privacy-preserving machine learning reduces exposure of sensitive training data.
Consent and data provenance matter when datasets include personal information.
Differential privacy adds carefully calibrated noise to protect individual records.
Federated learning trains across devices or servers without centralizing raw data.
Membership inference attacks try to determine whether data was in training.
Prompt injection tries to override instructions by placing commands in input data.
Adversarial examples are inputs designed to fool a model.
Data poisoning attacks corrupt training data to influence model behavior.
Model extraction attacks try to recreate a model by querying it.
Rate limits can reduce automated abuse of AI services.
MLOps applies software engineering practices to machine learning systems.
Model monitoring tracks performance after deployment.
Data drift occurs when production data changes from training data.
Concept drift occurs when the relationship between inputs and outputs changes.
Feature stores manage reusable machine learning features for training and serving.
Model registries track versions, metadata, and deployment status.
A/B tests compare model variants using live traffic or users.
Canary deployments expose a new model to a small traffic slice first.
Feature engineering transforms raw data into model-friendly inputs.
Categorical features often need encoding before many models can use them.
Normalization rescales values to make numeric features easier to compare.
Missing values can be imputed, modeled directly, or excluded depending on context.
Class imbalance can cause models to ignore rare but important outcomes.
Decision trees split data using feature rules that improve prediction purity.
Random forests combine many decision trees to improve generalization.
Gradient boosted trees build trees sequentially to correct earlier mistakes.
Support vector machines seek a boundary with the widest class margin.
K-nearest neighbors predicts using the labels of nearby training examples.
Naive Bayes applies Bayes' theorem with simplified independence assumptions.
Linear regression models a continuous target as a weighted sum of features.
Logistic regression estimates probabilities for classification tasks.
K-means groups points by assigning them to nearby centroids.
Hierarchical clustering builds nested groups of similar data points.
DBSCAN can find clusters with irregular shapes and mark outliers.
PCA projects data onto directions that explain the most variance.
t-SNE is often used to visualize high-dimensional data in two dimensions.
UMAP is a technique for visualizing and reducing high-dimensional data.
Convolution filters slide across images to detect local patterns.
Pooling layers reduce spatial size while preserving important visual signals.
Vision transformers apply transformer ideas to image patches.
Face recognition systems compare learned representations of facial features.
Pose estimation predicts key body points such as elbows, knees, and shoulders.
Automatic speech recognition converts spoken audio into text.
Text-to-speech systems synthesize spoken audio from written text.
Speaker diarization identifies who spoke when in an audio recording.
Wake word detection listens for a short phrase before activating an assistant.
Robots use perception, planning, and control to act in physical environments.
Simultaneous localization and mapping helps robots build maps while tracking position.
Path planning finds a route from a start point to a goal.
Computer vision helps robots identify objects, obstacles, and locations.
Autonomous vehicles combine sensors, prediction, planning, and control.
Sensor fusion combines data from multiple sensors into a single estimate.
Lidar measures distance by timing reflected laser pulses.
Control systems turn planned actions into steering, braking, or movement commands.
Knowledge graphs represent entities and relationships as connected nodes and edges.
Ontologies define concepts and relationships in a domain.
Reasoning systems can infer new facts from stored rules and relationships.
Multimodal models process more than one data type, such as text and images.
Image captioning generates natural language descriptions of images.
Visual question answering combines image understanding with language reasoning.
Audio-language models can connect speech, sound events, and text.
Transfer learning reuses knowledge from one task to improve another.
Fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model to a specific task or domain.
Feature extraction uses a pretrained model to create inputs for another model.
Pretraining on broad data can reduce the amount of task-specific data needed.
Epochs count how many times training has passed through the dataset.
Batch size controls how many examples are processed before a weight update.
Loss functions measure the gap between predictions and target values.
Checkpoints save model state so training or deployment can resume later.
Early stopping halts training when validation performance stops improving.
GPUs accelerate many AI workloads through parallel matrix operations.
TPUs are specialized processors designed for machine learning workloads.
Memory bandwidth can limit how fast large models run.
Quantization can reduce model size by storing weights with fewer bits.
Pruning removes less important model weights or connections.
Distillation trains a smaller model to mimic a larger model.
Sparse models activate only part of a network for some inputs.
Caching can speed up repeated model calls with shared context or results.
Batching multiple requests can improve hardware utilization during inference.
Instruction tuning trains models to follow human-written task instructions.
RLHF uses human preference feedback to improve model behavior.
Chain-of-thought prompting can encourage intermediate reasoning steps.
Tool calling lets a model request external functions for tasks it cannot do alone.
Function schemas help models produce structured tool arguments.
Structured outputs constrain responses to formats such as JSON.
Stop sequences tell text generation where to end.
Perplexity measures how surprised a language model is by text.
Machine translation automatically converts text from one language to another.
Sentiment analysis estimates the emotional polarity of text.
Text summarization condenses longer documents into shorter versions.
Stemming reduces words to rough root forms.
Lemmatization converts words to dictionary base forms.
Dependency parsing analyzes grammatical relationships between words.
Time-series forecasting predicts future values from ordered past observations.
Seasonality is a repeating pattern at regular time intervals.
Anomaly detection identifies unusual patterns that differ from expected behavior.
Recommendation systems predict items a user may find relevant.
Collaborative filtering uses patterns from similar users or items.
Content-based recommendation compares item features with user preferences.
Cold start problems happen when there is little data about new users or items.
Confusion matrices show correct and incorrect predictions by class.
ROC curves compare true positive rates and false positive rates.
Calibration measures whether predicted probabilities match real outcome frequencies.
Offline evaluation may not fully predict production performance.
Alan Turing proposed a famous test of machine intelligence in 1950.
The term artificial intelligence was popularized during the 1956 Dartmouth workshop.
Perceptrons were early neural networks used for simple pattern classification.
AI winters were periods of reduced funding and optimism in artificial intelligence.
Backpropagation helped renew interest in neural networks during the 1980s.
AI agents combine models with goals, memory, tools, or action loops.
Planning lets agents break larger goals into smaller steps.
Memory systems can help agents reuse information across interactions.
Tool use can let agents search, calculate, call APIs, or modify files.
Agent evaluation often checks both final answers and intermediate actions.
Good AI interfaces make uncertainty and limitations visible to users.
User feedback can improve prompts, retrieval, evaluations, and training data.
Autocomplete systems balance helpful suggestions with user control.
Explanations are more useful when they match the user's decision context.
Medical AI systems require careful validation before clinical use.
AI can help detect patterns in medical images such as X-rays and scans.
Clinical decision support should assist clinicians rather than replace judgment.
Fraud detection models look for unusual transaction patterns.
Credit scoring models must be monitored for fairness and regulatory compliance.
Algorithmic trading systems can react to market signals faster than humans.
AI tutors can adapt practice problems to a learner's progress.
Automated grading works best when rubrics are clear and outputs are reviewed.
AI can help search large scientific datasets for useful patterns.
Protein structure prediction is a major application of deep learning in biology.
Surrogate models approximate expensive simulations to speed up research.
Style transfer can apply the visual style of one image to another.
Music generation models learn patterns in melody, rhythm, and harmony.
AI writing tools can draft, rewrite, summarize, or adapt tone.
Generative tools still need human direction for taste, goals, and context.
Inference is the process of using a trained model to make predictions.
Latency measures how long a model takes to return a result.
Throughput measures how many requests a system can process over time.
Edge AI runs models on local devices instead of remote servers.
Serverless deployment can scale inference workloads based on demand.
Synthetic data is artificially generated data used for training or testing.
Data augmentation creates modified examples to improve model robustness.
Image augmentation can include crops, flips, rotations, and color changes.
Text augmentation can include paraphrasing, masking, or synonym replacement.
Autoencoders learn to compress data and reconstruct it.
Recurrent neural networks process sequences by carrying hidden state forward.
LSTMs were designed to better preserve information over long sequences.
Residual connections help very deep networks train more reliably.
Attention mechanisms let models focus on relevant parts of an input.
Matrix multiplication is a core operation in many neural network layers.
Vectors represent ordered numeric values such as features or embeddings.
Gradients point in the direction of steepest increase for a function.
Probability distributions describe how likely different outcomes are.
Entropy measures uncertainty in a probability distribution.
Uncertainty estimation helps users know when a model may be unreliable.
Out-of-distribution inputs differ meaningfully from the data a model saw before.
Fallback behavior defines what a system should do when confidence is low.
Evaluation datasets should include difficult edge cases, not only common examples.
Transparency helps users understand when they are interacting with AI.
Accountability means people and organizations remain responsible for AI outcomes.
Accessibility can improve when AI tools support translation, captions, and assistance.
Benchmark results are most useful when task design matches real use cases.
Human evaluation can capture qualities that automatic metrics miss.
Regression tests help catch model behavior changes after updates.
Reproducible training requires tracking code, data, parameters, and environment.
Experiment tracking records metrics and settings across model runs.
Rollback plans help teams recover when a deployed model performs poorly.
Latent spaces organize compressed representations that models can sample or edit.
Inpainting fills missing or selected regions of an image.
Outpainting extends an image beyond its original borders.
Classifier-free guidance can steer diffusion model outputs toward a prompt.
A model's parameters store learned statistical patterns from training.
Larger models can learn more patterns but often cost more to run.
Small language models can be useful when speed, cost, or privacy matters.
Domain adaptation can improve performance on specialized language and tasks.
Evaluation prompts should be separated from prompts used during development.
Source citations help users inspect evidence behind generated answers.
Fresh retrieval can reduce reliance on stale model knowledge.
Poor document chunking can hide relevant context from a retriever.
Least-privilege tool access limits what an AI system can do if misused.
Output filtering can catch some unsafe content before it reaches users.
